blindSummary: Same-sex conduct has been criminalised in this country since 2009 (2 years), and the head of state himself has called for mob violence: in December 2023 he said LGBT people should be taken to a stadium and stoned because that is what they deserve - the remarks were condemned by an international rights group as stoking fear, and the leading domestic rights group (in exile) called them a call to lynching. There is no legal gender recognition, no community infrastructure (the oldest rights group works from exile), and arbitrary detention is routine.
blindOutOfScope: Presidential incitement is documented by an international human-rights organisation (Jan 2024).
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation (Jan 2024): reports the head of state's call to stone homosexuals, which stoked fear among LGBT people in this country, and urges the ruling party to renounce persecution.

An exiled independent media outlet (Jan 2024): after the head of state called for homosexuals to be stoned, LGBTQ people in this country reported terror; the leading domestic human-rights organisation, operating in exile, called the remarks a call for the lynching of LGBTQ people. Members of two LGBTQ associations, speaking anonymously, described the remarks as a real licence to kill them. Same-sex relations are criminalised here.

A foreign government's 2015 human-rights report on this country: documents the country's crisis (extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detention, media shutdowns) and includes the section on acts of violence and discrimination against LGBT persons - same-sex conduct criminalised since 2009, with arrests and harassment documented.
A foreign government's archived 2009 human-rights report on this country: covers the year the penal code criminalised same-sex conduct; documents discrimination against gays and lesbians.

A foreign government's 2010 human-rights report on this country: lists discrimination against gays and lesbians among common human-rights abuses, alongside security-force killings, torture and harsh prison conditions.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on this country: documents torture, extrajudicial executions, prolonged pretrial detention, and discrimination against LGBT persons under the criminalised framework.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised since 2009 — the vehicle by which trans people (legally their birth sex) are prosecuted; also a direct risk for trans visitors with partners.
